title: Session-expiry notification is buried under HTML parse-error toasts on a concurrent burst
product: @vc-shell/framework / Marketplace Vendor Portal (separate product, not the storefront)
linked_fix_pr_note: The ticket had NO comments at all — no dev note, no PR reference. Located from main's history.
environment: vc-shell main @ 324cd9b09 (= v2.5.0) + deployed vcmp-dev vendor-portal build 22260 (2026-08-24)
agent_used: none — no browser agent dispatched, deliberately; see live_axis. Unit probes and source tracing run inline.
design_decisions_credited: Gated on the expiry latch, so a login page seen while nobody is signed in stays an expected answer rather than a session death.
A 401 is deliberately returned unchanged, because its body is not a document so nothing tries to parse markup.

red_failures: treats an API call answered with an HTML login page as an expired session
fails the request instead of handing the login page's HTML to the caller  <- the core fix
recognises the login page by its URL when the content type is absent
acts once for a burst of concurrent requests that all land on the login page  <- the burst
unit.scoping_note: Both source files (interceptors/index.ts + utilities/sessionExpiration.ts) revert together — the interceptor's throw needs the SessionExpiredError class the same PR introduced, so reverting one alone would not compile. useAsync/index.ts was NOT reverted: its notify guard is pre-existing (PR #291 touched only useAsync.docs.md).
unit.coverage_note: 15 tests across both branches. Beyond the 4 above: 'still returns a 401 response to the caller', 'leaves an ordinary JSON response alone', 'does not sign out on a 403', 'leaves an HTML response that was not redirected alone', 'does not act on a login page while nobody is signed in', 'does not fail the sign-in request itself', plus 5 401-handling cases incl. 'handles concurrent 401s from the same dead session exactly once'. Every design decision and all five negative guards are pinned.

deploy_gate.bundle: vc-shell-vendors22260.js carries 'SessionExpiredError' x1 and the full message 'The session has expired, so this request was not completed' x1; the -framework facade chunk has 0 of both, as expected. looksLikeLoginPage / markSessionExpired absent — module-local names, minified; the class name and message survive as string literals.
deploy_gate.independent_live_corroboration: The VCST-5667 verification run earlier the same day hit, on a first sign-in attempt against vcmp-dev, 'Authentication error: The session has expired, so this request was not completed.' — verbatim this fix's SessionExpiredError default, observed by a different agent on an unrelated ticket. So the class is deployed and reaches a user-visible surface.

notes: RETRACTED (my error, not the fix's): my first pass claimed the notificationId de-duplication cited in useAsync.docs.md 'does not exist as described' and that the collapse rested on the !isSessionExpired() suppression alone. Both false. useAsync/index.ts:65 derives the id FROM THE ERROR MESSAGE (`async-error-${message.slice(0,80)}`), showNotification preserves a supplied id, and useContainer actions.add() de-duplicates on it (`if (!exists) push`, no else branch). So N identical-message errors produce exactly ONE toast and the interceptor's own comment is correct. How I got it wrong: I traced showNotification -> appendInstance (which only mounts the per-position container) and stopped, missing actions.add() — a sibling in the same file. Same shape of error as VCST-5667: concluding without checking the layer below.

Two further real mechanisms I also missed: (a) the latch has FOUR consumers — interceptors:166 sets it, :194 is this fix, useAsync:64 suppresses the toast, and shell/components/error-interceptor/interceptor.ts:56 suppresses the BLADE ERROR BANNER; (b) the toast is deferred via setTimeout(0) and registered through setPendingErrorNotification so ErrorInterceptor can cancelPendingErrorNotification when onErrorCaptured fires — a third de-duplication path.

SCOPE GAP IN THE FIX ITSELF (unchanged): the ticket's Actual described TWO things — four extra parse-error toasts AND the expiry toast being 'visible ~2.6s and not the topmost/most prominent message'. The fix addresses the first only. Toast ordering/prominence is untouched and not testable at unit level.

OBSERVATION TO RECONCILE (unchanged): the suite pins 'does not fail the sign-in request itself', yet the VCST-5667 run saw the SessionExpiredError message surface DURING sign-in prefixed 'Authentication error:'. Likely a stale latch from a prior session. One sighting, no repro, not called a defect.

live_axis.status: BLOCKED BY TOOLING — no browser agent dispatched, deliberately
reasons: The ticket itself records that this platform cannot produce the 302->HTML trigger naturally (established during VCST-5598); the original repro was fault-injected.

Playwright MCP exposes NO route-interception tool — there is no browser_route. The only way to install a route handler is browser_run_code_unsafe, which hooks/enforce-real-user.mjs blocks, and the documented /* @allow-eval */ opt-in is scoped to 'UI-FIX / DEBUG DOM experiment, NOT for test runs'.
The naturally reachable expiry (clearing the HttpOnly cookies) yields a 401 — a DIFFERENT branch, which this fix deliberately leaves unchanged. It can neither confirm nor refute the defect.
live_axis.rationale: Dispatching an agent would have burned a session on a branch it structurally could not reach. Evidence relied on instead: the unit RED->GREEN incl. the burst case, the deployed-bundle markers, and the independent live sighting of the message.
live_axis.how_to_close: Extend hooks/enforce-real-user.mjs's allowlist for page.route / unrouteAll fault injection — the clean fix the hook's own guidance points at. THIRD time in this session that gap has bounded a verification.

The 401 branch was not exercised live, though it is unit-pinned.

step_a_natural_half.burst: 8 /api/ calls in TWO waves; the concurrent wave is exactly the six the ticket names (seller/products/search, orders/search, quote/search, seller/offers/search, rating, reviews/search), all 200 application/json. The extra two are a later re-fetch of the Orders and Offers widgets. The ticket's '6-call concurrent burst' rationale holds — refined, not contradicted.
step_a_natural_half.concurrency_evidence: Two independent lines, no scripting: response Date headers place a 1146ms and a 648ms request in the same one-second window (1794ms cannot complete sequentially); and requests 187-192 share a Cloudflare cf-ray tick prefix a30b58c198 that the two later calls do not. Caveat: proves in-flight overlap, not same-tick dispatch — Playwright's log has no per-request initiation timestamp.
step_a_natural_half.healthy_path: Zero toasts; role=status container present and empty; no Unexpected token '<' anywhere; 0 console errors.
step_a_natural_half.fixed_code_present: Confirmed by fetching the served asset (no page evaluation): vc-shell-vendors22260.js carries the SessionExpiredError class verbatim with the module-level latch and its guard adjacent.
step_a_natural_half.four_oh_one_message: The 401 branch is separately worded, in the OTHER chunk: 'Access Denied: Your session has expired or you do not have the necessary permissions.'
step_a_natural_half.natural_session_death: NOT OBSERVED — zero 401s across the session, so the 401 branch stays live-unverified (unit-pinned only).
step_a_natural_half.env_noise_calibration: The 500s recorded on earlier runs today did NOT reproduce: /pushNotificationHub/negotiate returned 200, seller/offers/search returned 200 twice. Those earlier failures look session-specific, not stable characteristics of vcmp-dev.
